title: Tipu’s Tiger
note: The South Kensington Museum was renamed the Victoria and Albert Museum. The journey shows selected documented stages, not every building move.

title: Bedchamber Sword
note: Publicly documented sale is not proof of present physical location. Intermediate private ownership is described in the auction provenance. Auction provenance records Baird family descent and a 2003 sale before the 2023 auction. The journey cards omit that intermediate sale.

title: Throne Tiger Head
note: Associated with the Grand Vestibule at Windsor Castle. A collection location does not guarantee public access on a particular day.

title: Throne Finial
note: The detailed accession record identifies Richard Wellesley. A new display at Powis Castle opened in February 2026.

title: Koh-i-Noor
note: Image: public-domain 1851 engraving, not a photograph of the current cut. Lahore is now in Pakistan; Punjab was part of historical India.

title: Ranjit Singh’s Throne
note: Current catalogue gives about 1805–1810; older labels differ. Official structured record: https://api.vam.ac.uk/v2/museumobject/O18891. Lahore is now in Pakistan.

title: Huma Bird
note: Display status is not confirmed. Photograph reproduced by thetipusultan.com from Royal Collection imagery; no open reuse licence confirmed.

title: Royal Tent Panels
note: Attribution to Tipu’s use is qualified by the collection. The photograph shows the museum installation of the panels.

title: Tipu’s War Turban
note: The museum article identifies the Global Role gallery display.

title: Tipu’s Amulet Case
note: The removal account is attributed to the museum catalogue, not treated as independently witnessed fact. Exact intervening movements and current display are not documented here.

title: Jewelled Khanjar
note: The separate collection record was intermittently unavailable. The working museum article explicitly includes this dagger. Display status is not confirmed.

title: Bahadur Shah’s Crown
note: Post-conquest dispersal through auction is distinguished from direct battlefield seizure. Photo reproduced on TrueGemstone’s Crown Jewelry article; no open reuse licence confirmed.

title: Baird’s Trophy Musket
note: Recorded as kept by David Baird as a trophy after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
description: Long Indian musket with narrow steel barrel, dark wood stock and silver filigree fittings, gold at muzzle.

title: Bareilly Shield
note: Recorded as recovered from a warrior at the Battle of Bareilly.
description: Round dark hide shield, four central silver bosses and crescent upper ornament.

title: Lucknow Filigree Box
note: Base inscription records Loot from Lucknow March 1858; palace attribution is uncertain.
description: Oval silver-gilt lidded box with intricate openwork scrolling filigree.

title: Awadh Royal Coins
note: Two coins counted as one documented group.
description: Two aged gold coins bearing the Awadh royal emblem; one grouped object.

title: Seringapatam Axe
note: Catalogue identifies capture at Seringapatam.
description: Fin-shaped steel axe blade on a dark wooden shaft with brass bands, entire axe diagonal.

title: Captured Royal Staff
note: Said to have belonged to Tipu; later converted into a British drum-major staff.
description: Long dark wood staff with bulbous chased silver head and silver chains spiralling shaft.

title: Imperial Dessert Stand
note: Taken from Bahadur Shah’s collection after the fall of Delhi.
description: White china dessert stand with blue ribbon-like border and red gold imperial central emblem.

title: Awadh Royal Umbrella
note: Removed from Wajid Ali Shah’s palace by P. Blake.
description: Golden yellow silk ceremonial parasol with brocade and beads on reddish wood pole, full object.

title: Delhi Gong
note: Taken by the 61st Regiment; inscription’s day differs from the capture date.
description: Large circular aged brass gong with small centre boss and incised inscription, hanging cord.

title: Shah Zaman’s Standard
note: Surviving fragment of a captured regimental standard.
description: A fragile rectangular yellow gold silk banner fragment with silver gold embroidered foliate patterns.

title: Royal Boat Paddle Blade
note: Removed by Thomas Bland Strange from the Nawab of Awadh’s state boat.
description: Long silver-plated ceremonial paddle with fish-scale blade and floral bands, diagonal full length.

title: Imperial Bed Panels
note: Two carved plaques recorded as taken from Bahadur Shah’s bed; one group.
description: Two dark mahogany carved panels of reclining lions, symmetrical paired reliefs.

title: Kashmir Gate Keys
note: Three keys taken by N. C. Waterfield on 14 September 1857.
description: Three large antique iron gate keys with incised geometric decoration, arranged diagonally.

title: A Sepoy’s Signet Ring
note: Recorded as taken from a dead sepoy by a Naval Brigade officer.
description: Small silver signet ring with flat inscribed oval face and cross-hatched shoulders.

title: Imperial Fly Whisk
note: Taken from Bahadur Shah’s palace by an unidentified British soldier.
description: Long silver spiral fluted handle with dense golden cream animal-hair plume, horizontal.

title: Walking-stick Handle
note: Inscription records removal from Tipu’s palace.
description: Cream bone walking stick with four slender ribbed columns and gold collar, entire object diagonal.

title: Kunwar Singh’s Mace
note: Said to have been taken from Kunwar Singh by George Godfrey Pearse.
description: Tall ceremonial silver mace with spherical fluted head and engraved shaft.

title: Kunwar Singh’s Chauri
note: Recorded as taken from Kunwar Singh; the attribution is qualified.
description: Ornate silver fly whisk with long pale flowing horsehair plume and chased handle.

title: Kunwar Singh’s Chob
note: Recorded as taken from Kunwar Singh; see catalogue and research on conflicting inscriptions.
description: Long silver ceremonial club terminating in a sculpted tiger head, curved at top.

title: Tiger-stripe Blunderbuss
note: The Met explicitly records the weapon’s removal as booty in 1799.
description: Indian flintlock blunderbuss, flared steel barrel gold hunting tiger damascening, brown wooden stock silver tiger-stripe fittings.

title: Mail-and-plate Helmet
note: Museum records seizure at Seringapatam.
description: Domed helmet made of twelve radial scalloped iron plates joined by chain mail, with chain-mail cheek and neck guards.

title: Tipu’s Dream Register
note: British Library curator article republished by Scroll; register found by Kirkpatrick after the palace fell.
description: Small unassuming aged manuscript notebook open to sparse handwritten Persian lines, cream pages with dark brown cover, no invented readable quotations.

title: Cat’s-eye Ring
note: An attached label says it was taken from Tipu’s finger; this is an attributed history.
description: Heavy gold ring with a large smooth cabochon yellow-green chrysoberyl catseye stone.

title: Silver Perfume Casket
note: UCL object study follows the casket from Tipu’s palace through Fraser family ownership.
description: Small Indian silver perfume casket with a domed lobed lid and ornate floral engraving, supported on small feet.

title: Tiger-hilt Sword
note: National Trust discusses the 1799 spoils and a Grant letter that may refer to this sword.
description: Blued-steel curved sword with fine gold inlay and gold tiger-head hilt, full sword diagonal.

title: Timur Ruby
note: A spinel, not a ruby. The Lahore treasury stone was presented to Victoria after annexation; later British necklace setting is not itself Indian loot.
description: Large irregular smooth deep red spinel with finely engraved historic Persian inscriptions in modest gold setting, isolated stone not full necklace.

title: Lahore Diamond
note: The pendant stone came from the Lahore treasury; the complete necklace was made in Britain later.
description: Large pear-shaped brilliant diamond pendant in simple silver collet setting, isolated pendant only.

title: Awadh Ceremonial Sword
note: Museum says probably made in Awadh and likely acquired as war loot; qualified on stamp.
description: Ceremonial curved sword with gilt floral hilt and dark scabbard decorated with broad chased gold mounts.

title: Red Fort Inlay Panels
note: Captain John Jones removed panels in 1857; returned by South Kensington Museum in 1903. This is a group, not a claim that all removed pieces returned.
description: One white marble architectural panel inlaid with coloured stone vines, birds and a central musician figure representing Orpheus, rectangular.

title: Mughal Throne Chairs
note: Royal Collection crown history records two throne chairs bought from Tytler after Delhi conquest. Counted as one group.
description: A pair of nineteenth-century Mughal gilded throne chairs with openwork floral backs and red cushions, two identical court chairs.

title: Sher Singh’s Girdle
note: Lahore treasury dismantled by the East India Company in 1849; girdle subsequently presented to Victoria.
description: A long articulated waist belt with nineteen graduated rectangular emeralds surrounded by diamond borders in gold settings, arranged in a shallow arc.

title: Nassak Diamond
note: Surrendered by Bajirao II and sent to Britain as war spoil. The Peshwa had previously removed it from Trimbakeshwar; British troops did not directly take it from the shrine.
description: A transparent colourless large rectangular emerald-cut diamond with clipped corners; current cut, no blue colour.

title: French Royal Bust
note: Gift to Tipu’s ambassadors; removed during the 1799 looting and acquired by John Adamson Rice. Acquired by the V&A in 1983.
description: White biscuit porcelain bust of Marie Antoinette, curled powdered hair and draped shoulders, on a dark blue and gold cylindrical porcelain pedestal.

title: Presentation Sword
note: Eastern European sword kept in Tipu’s treasury, explicitly catalogued as booty from Seringapatam.
description: Late sixteenth century Eastern European curved presentation sword with ornate gilt crossguard and green velvet gold-mounted scabbard.

title: Tipu’s Sporting Gun
note: Gun made for Tipu; sent to Cornwallis after the fall of Seringapatam. A 2023 export-bar notice does not establish its present location.
description: Long flintlock sporting gun with dark brown wood stock, polished steel barrel and intricate gold tiger-stripe inlay, full length diagonal.

title: Tipu’s Book of Kings
note: Sixteenth-century Iranian manuscript with an Indian binding, appropriated from Tipu’s library and sent to Cambridge by the Company in 1806.
description: Large thick manuscript in red leather binding with gold medallions and triangular fore-edge flap, slightly open revealing decorated cream pages.
